title: Flat bounded cohomology gives finite Tor amplitude
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and its residue field $k=R/(\varpi)$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $V$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme] weakly contractible for its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], meaning that evaluation on $V$ sends every epimorphism of sheaves of sets to a surjection. Put $B=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(R/\varpi^n)_V$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], and let $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(B))$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category] be derived complete for its coefficient quotient tower [def-weil-derived-complete]. Write $k_V$ for the constant sheaf of residue fields [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and $K_1=K\otimes^L_B k_V$, the derived reduction modulo $\varpi$ [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction] (here $k_V=(R/\varpi)_V$). Suppose $a\leq b$ are integers, $H^q(K_1)=0$ for $q\notin[a,b]$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves], and each $H^q(K_1)$ is locally constant with finite-dimensional $k$-vector-space local models [def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf]. Then for every object $U\to V$ of $V_{\mathrm{proet}}$, every sheaf $L$ of $k_U$-modules, and every $i\notin[a,b]$, one has
$$H^i\bigl((K_1|_U)\otimes^L_{k_U}L\bigr)=0,$$
where $k_U=k_V|_U$ and restriction is to the localized site [def-pur-localized-ringed-site, def-weil-pbc-ringed-site-derived-restriction]. Thus the residue complex has Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ on every slice, not just after evaluation on $V$.
